text.en: 3. Exit paths

The money comes back through a trade sale, and that route is neither near nor certain. Forge shows no confidential filing and no S-1 activity for ZaiNar, and no available secondary price, as of 20 August 2026 [S5]. A confidential filing is the first visible step toward a listing; its absence means a 2027 or 2028 listing is not on the table, and an exit realistically sits in 2029 or later. Between February 2026 and that exit there is no interim mark of any kind: no quoted secondary, no independent enterprise value at Preqin, no filings record at Tracxn [S5, S9, S6]. Capital committed here is locked and unpriced for four years or more [S5].

items.en: Trade sale to a network or enterprise-infrastructure incumbent is the realistic route, and the constraint is that the buyers are also the competitors. Ericsson, Nokia, Cisco, HPE Aruba and Zebra are the named candidates, and they are the same set that can bundle competing positioning into infrastructure contracts customers already pay for, at marginal cost [S4]. A buyer who can ship the capability inside its own release cycle negotiates for patents and engineers, not for a growth platform. Ericsson launched integrated 5G Advanced location services in January 2026 and demonstrated decimeter-level accuracy with MediaTek over a commercial network in August 2026, without proprietary middleware [S4] — that is the acquirer telling the market it has an alternative to buying.

An independent listing is possible but distant, and the constraint is scale. A software-track infrastructure company generally needs recurring revenue past roughly $200M, with growth and margin together clearing the Rule of 40, before public markets will take it. ZaiNar discloses no revenue at all [S4], so the base case's $200M of 2030 revenue is the first year in which a listing even becomes a conversation [C8]. That is the good outcome, not the expected one, and it arrives at the end of the holding period rather than inside it.

A patent-led outcome is the floor, and the constraint is that floors are cheap. Nine years of stealth produced 100+ filings and 90+ issued patents by company account, with US10455350B2 publicly viewable [S1, S14]. No independent claim-scope review exists, so what the estate fetches in a distressed sale is unknown. The bear case assumes $400M for patents and team [C7], which is well below the corroborated $579.37M mark of 2021 [S5, S6].

text.en: Follow the arithmetic on the non-premium outcome, because it is the one an incumbent buyer is most likely to offer. A $400M trade sale for patents and people, after 30% dilution, returns $400M × 0.70 = $280M against $1,000M invested, or 0.28x — a loss of about 72 cents on the dollar, at an IRR of −27% a year over four years [C7]. Note what that loss does not require: it does not require the technology to fail. It requires only that standardized network positioning becomes good enough and that the memoranda do not convert. Both are live conditions today rather than speculative ones.

There is one structural protection worth naming, and it is thinner than it sounds. Forge records the 2021 Series A as carrying a 1.0x non-participating liquidation preference, meaning preferred holders take their money back before common in a sale but must choose between that and converting to equity [S5]. No preference terms for the February 2026 round are published anywhere. A buyer at the $1B+ mark therefore cannot tell where in the stack the new money sits, which matters most precisely in the $400M outcome where the stack decides who is paid.

What to check: the binding-versus-memorandum split inside the $450M+ commercial aggregate, the liquidation preference and participation terms attaching to the February 2026 round, and whether any carrier agreement has been signed since the February 2026 statement that partnerships were weeks away.

Taken together, the price and the exit point the same way. The $1B+ mark has no revenue denominator, and the only corroborated prior mark makes the step-up look ordinary rather than exceptional [C1, C3]. This dimension scores 3 of 8.
On the way out, no IPO signal exists and the most plausible acquirers are the incumbents best placed to build the capability instead [S4, S5]. This dimension scores 2 of 4.
1. The center of gravity

One risk carries everything else here: the headline commercial figure cannot be read as revenue. ZaiNar says it holds more than $450M in "contracts and memoranda of understanding" as of February 2026, restated as $500M+ in April 2026 [S1, S3]. A memorandum of understanding is a written statement of intent that neither side is obliged to perform; a signed contract is. No source splits the two, and no customer is named [S4]. Every other risk in the register is a variation on that gap or a consequence of it.

It outranks the price risk because it determines the price risk. A $1B+ mark on $200M of eventual revenue is expensive but survivable — the base case still returns 1.26x over four years [C8]. The same mark on a book that turns out to be mostly intent is not: the bear case returns 0.28x, roughly 28 cents on the dollar [C7]. The two outcomes differ by a factor of four and a half, and the only thing separating them is a disclosure that has not been made in the seven months since launch.

If it lands, the investment is a patent sale. A network incumbent buys the estate and the engineering team, the site licences never scale, and the position ends below the mark it was bought at. That is why the recommendation is a pass at this price rather than a wait-and-see: the fact that would settle the question is cheap for the company to publish and has not been published.
2. Risk register
Risk 1: The headline commercial figure cannot be read as revenue, because it blends signed contracts with non-binding memoranda and names no customer.
text.zh: 风险 1：头部商业数字无法视为收入，因为它把已签合同与不具约束力的谅解备忘录混在一起，且未指名任何客户。

rows.en: Risk Type
Commercialization
Verdict
The headline commercial figure cannot be read as revenue, because it blends signed contracts with non-binding memoranda and names no customer.
Impact
If the binding share is small, the bear case becomes the base case and the position returns 0.28x — a loss of roughly three quarters of the money even though the technology works [C7].
Why it matters

The company's one commercial number is an aggregate of "contracts and memoranda of understanding" — more than $450M at the 19 February 2026 launch, restated as more than $500M in the 20 April 2026 Tokyo announcement [S1, S3]. A memorandum of understanding records an intention to work together and binds neither party to buy anything. A contract does. The two are added together and published as one figure, and no source separates them; Sacra states plainly that as of August 2026 there was no public split of binding backlog from non-binding memoranda, no named commercial customer and no independent field benchmark [S4]. Dividing the $1B mark by that aggregate gives 2.2x [C3], which measures the quality of a disclosure rather than the value of a business. For a software-infrastructure company at this stage, the normal disclosure is a customer count, a top-three logo list and a contracted backlog figure with a term attached; investors in this category routinely see all three before a unicorn mark. None appear here. For the risk not to bite, the binding share would have to be large enough to produce real 2030 revenue — the base case needs about $200M, and at that level the position still only returns 1.26x, about 6% a year [C8]. If instead most of the aggregate lapses, a trade sale for patents and team at $400M returns 0.28x after 30% dilution [C7]. The commercial disclosure, not the physics, decides which of those two numbers the investor gets.
What we watch

A named production customer with a site count, and a contracted-backlog figure stated separately from memoranda. Neither has appeared in the seven months of public record since the February 2026 launch, and neither appeared in the April 2026 Tokyo release, which restated the blended figure instead [S1, S3, S4].
Mitigation
No structural mitigation exists. No BSH vehicle or terms are on file, so there is no milestone tranche, no revenue-based conversion and no information right that would force the split into the open.
Likelihood
High: the split has been withheld through two company announcements and one independent vendor review, which is itself evidence about what it would show.
Risk Rating
9/10: it alone moves the outcome from 1.26x to 0.28x, and it is unresolvable from outside the company.

text.en: Risk 2: The entry price has no denominator: a $1B+ mark sits on revenue that has never been disclosed.
text.zh: 风险 2：入场价格没有分母——10 亿美元以上的估值建立在从未披露的收入之上。

rows.en: Risk Type
Valuation & exit
Verdict
The entry price has no denominator: a $1B+ mark sits on revenue that has never been disclosed.
Impact
The base case returns 1.26x over four years, about 6% a year [C8] — thin for an illiquid private position, and every point of multiple compression comes out of principal first.
Why it matters

A valuation multiple is a price divided by something the business earns. Here the numerator is the $1B+ post-money announced on 19 February 2026 [S1] and the denominator does not exist: no revenue, annual recurring revenue or bookings figure appears in any source, and Preqin's enterprise-value, revenue-multiple and EBITDA-multiple fields for this asset are blank [S4, S9]. The registry's ~$24M ARR is a self-labelled design-mock placeholder with no document behind it and is excluded from every number here [S19]. So the price cannot be tested against earnings power at all [C3]. What can be tested is the step-up between priced rounds. The corroborated Series A post-money was $579.37M on 31 August 2021 [S5, S6]; $1,000M ÷ $579.37M = 1.73x over roughly 4.4 years, which compounds at about 13% a year [C1]. That is the return profile of a credit fund, not of a breakout technology asset, and it is the only mark-to-mark evidence available. Judged against the entry price rather than an invented bar: at the $1B mark the base case pays 1.26x over four years, or about 6% annually [C8]; at an $800M entry the same 9x exit on $200M of 2030 revenue pays 1.6x, and at $1.2B it pays 1.1x. So a 20% swing in entry price moves the outcome between a modest gain and roughly breaking even. With no denominator, the investor is paying for a story and absorbing the first loss on any repricing.
What we watch

A disclosed revenue or ARR figure with a period attached, and a priced round or secondary trade at a stated share price. Forge showed no available secondary price and limited activity as of 20 August 2026 [S5].
Mitigation
No structural mitigation exists. Without a vehicle, terms or a disclosed denominator, the price is taken as given and there is no valuation floor other than the 2021 mark of $579.37M [S5].
Likelihood
High: the absence of a revenue figure is a present fact, not a forecast — the mark is already unanchored today.
Risk Rating
9/10: it caps the base case at 6% a year even when execution succeeds, so price alone can turn a working company into a poor investment.

text.en: Risk 3: Standardization can absorb the product, because RAN-native positioning is already shipping and already accurate.
text.zh: 风险 3：标准化可能吞掉该产品，因为无线接入网原生定位已经在出货，且精度已经够用。

rows.en: Risk Type
Moat & defensibility
Verdict
Standardization can absorb the product, because RAN-native positioning is already shipping and already accurate.
Impact
If 3GPP Release 18/19 positioning becomes good enough, the patent estate is worth what an acquirer pays for defensive IP, which is the $400M bear exit rather than a revenue multiple [C7].
Why it matters

3GPP is the body that writes the mobile standards every carrier and handset maker implements. When a capability enters a release, it ships inside equipment customers already buy, at no separate price. Ericsson launched integrated 5G Advanced location services in January 2026 and demonstrated decimeter-level accuracy with MediaTek over a commercial network in August 2026, without proprietary middleware in the path [S4]. Decimeter means tenths of a metre — the same order of precision ZaiNar's sub-meter claim occupies. The company-type test for this kind of infrastructure asset is the absorption window: assume the standard or the incumbent ships the capability free in its next major release, and ask whether the company survives on its own. On the evidence here it survives only if the accuracy gap is large enough that carriers choose to resell ZaiNar rather than replace it — which is also the condition under which the licensing model works at all [S4]. The patent estate is real: 100+ filings and 90+ issued with zero rejections in phase-based time synchronization and network-computed positioning as of February 2026, with US10455350B2 publicly viewable [S1, S14]. What it does not do is stop a standardized method that designs around the claims, and no independent claim-scope review exists. If the standard wins, the outcome is the bear path: a trade sale for the IP and the team at $400M, which after 30% dilution returns 0.28x, a 27% annual loss over four years [C7]. The estate is what stops that going to zero; it is not what makes the case.
What we watch

Release 18/19 positioning accuracy published in commercial carrier deployments rather than lab demonstrations, and any ZaiNar licence or settlement asserting its claims against a standardized method. Neither exists in the public record as of September 2026 [S4, S14].
Mitigation
The issued patent estate is the real mitigant: it converts a lost product race into a defensive IP sale, which is what puts a $400M floor under the bear case rather than zero [S1, C7].
Likelihood
Medium: the capability is demonstrated but not yet broadly deployed at commercial accuracy, so the timing is open while the direction is not.
Risk Rating
8/10: it removes the product economics entirely and leaves only IP value, though the IP floor keeps it short of total loss.

text.en: Risk 4: Incumbents give away positioning inside licences customers already pay for, which caps how much of the market is genuinely contestable.
text.zh: 风险 4：老牌厂商把定位功能免费塞进客户已经在付费的许可中，这限制了真正可争夺的市场规模。

rows.en: Risk Type
Competition
Verdict
Incumbents give away positioning inside licences customers already pay for, which caps how much of the market is genuinely contestable.
Impact
The addressable pool narrows to precision-sensitive workflows, so the $50.10B 2031 category ceiling overstates what a standalone vendor can win [C6].
Why it matters

Cisco Spaces and HPE Aruba already carry location features inside wireless network licences enterprises buy anyway, and Nokia and Ericsson can attach positioning to infrastructure contracts at marginal cost [S4]. A buyer weighing a separate software licence against a feature already included does not compare capability; it compares the incremental price against zero. That is the structural problem with a standalone software layer sitting on someone else's radios. The market figure most often quoted is MarketsandMarkets' indoor location total — $18.35B in 2026 growing to $50.10B by 2031 at 22.3% a year [S10, C6]. That total includes the tags, anchors and installation services a no-new-hardware model does not sell, and part of what remains is already bundled free in the incumbent licences above. The contestable slice is therefore the workflows where bundled accuracy is not good enough: surgical instrument tracking, active construction sites, autonomous equipment coordination. No published report sizes that slice, so its size is an assumption rather than a figure. For the risk not to bite, ZaiNar's precision has to be materially better than the bundled option and the customer's process has to need that precision. Where both hold, the company sells at a premium; where either fails, it competes against free. The practical effect lands on the revenue path: the base case assumes $200M of 2030 revenue [C8], a small share of even the narrowed pool, and that modest assumption is the honest response to a ceiling that overstates the opportunity.
What we watch

Competitive displacements where a customer replaces or supplements Cisco Spaces or HPE Aruba location with ZaiNar, and the price per site those deals carry. No such deal is named in any source as of September 2026 [S4].
Mitigation

The Arm Total Design ecosystem seat gives a silicon-level channel that sits beside direct enterprise sales, reaching devices instead of competing for the network licence [S16]. No contract value or committed volume is attached to it.
Likelihood
High: the bundling is already in market, not prospective.
Risk Rating
7/10: it shrinks the reachable market rather than removing it, but it pushes achievable revenue well below any share-of-category path.

text.en: Risk 5: Distribution rests on a carrier channel that was promised within weeks in February 2026 and has not been announced since.
text.zh: 风险 5：分销依赖于 2026 年 2 月承诺数周内落地、此后再无公布的运营商渠道。

rows.en: Risk Type
Concentration
Verdict
Distribution rests on a carrier channel that was promised within weeks in February 2026 and has not been announced since.
Impact
Without it, every enterprise is sold one at a time through network qualification and a paid pilot, which is what holds the base case to $200M of 2030 revenue [C8].
Why it matters

The launch release said major carrier and enterprise partnerships would be announced in the coming weeks [S1]. Seven months later no source confirms one [S4]. A carrier channel matters more here than in most software businesses because the product runs on the carrier's own radios: one agreement can put the software across thousands of sites at once, while the alternative is a three-step enterprise sale — network qualification, then a paid pilot, then a production site licence [S4]. That motion is slow by construction, and ZaiNar runs it with roughly 50-60 employees [S4, S8]. The arithmetic follows directly. A three-step sale closing site by site is what makes $200M of 2030 revenue the reasonable base assumption rather than the $500M the bull case needs [C8, C9]. The gap between those two revenue lines, at 9x and 12x respectively, is the gap between a 1.26x return and a 4.20x return [C8, C9]. So the carrier channel is not an adjacent detail; it is most of the difference between the two outcomes. For the risk not to bite, a named carrier agreement with a deployment scope has to be signed. The pattern worth noting is that a company willing to publish a $450M+ commercial aggregate and a patent count has not published the partnership it pre-announced, which is information in itself.
What we watch

A named carrier agreement with a stated deployment footprint, and whether the Tokyo Metropolitan Government market-entry selection of April 2026 converts into a paid municipal deployment with a disclosed value [S3].
Mitigation

The investor register — SoftBank, Samsung, AME Cloud Ventures, Future Ventures — is carrier- and silicon-adjacent capital that can open those doors [S8]. Introductions are not contracts, and none has produced an announced agreement.
Likelihood
Medium: the relationships and the ecosystem seat are real, but the promised announcement has slipped by seven months.
Risk Rating
6/10: it separates the base path from the bull path rather than profit from loss.

text.en: Risk 6: There is no exit on the horizon, and the likeliest buyers are the same incumbents that can build the capability themselves.
text.zh: 风险 6：退出路径尚不可见，而最可能的买家正是那些完全可以自己造出同等能力的老牌厂商。

rows.en: Risk Type
Valuation & exit
Verdict
There is no exit on the horizon, and the likeliest buyers are the same incumbents that can build the capability themselves.
Impact
With no IPO filing signal and no quoted secondary price as of 20 August 2026, capital is locked up for four years or more with no interim mark [S5].
Why it matters

Two exits are available to a private infrastructure company: a listing or a trade sale. On the listing path, Forge shows no confidential filing and no S-1 activity as of 20 August 2026, and no available secondary price with limited trading activity [S5]. For a software-track company the usual listing bar is revenue past $200M with disciplined growth; ZaiNar has disclosed no revenue at all, so a 2029 or later listing is the realistic earliest window and the four-year hold assumed throughout is optimistic rather than conservative. On the trade-sale path, the plausible buyers are Ericsson, Nokia, Cisco, HPE Aruba and Zebra — the same set Sacra identifies as able to bundle competing positioning into existing infrastructure contracts at marginal cost [S4]. A buyer who can build the capability negotiates for the patents and the team, not for a revenue multiple. That is exactly the $400M bear exit, which returns 0.28x after dilution [C7]. Meanwhile the position cannot be marked or sold: no secondary bid exists, so there is no interim price to report and no way to act on a view that changes in 2028. The consequence for the return is that the investor holds the full four years of the distribution described in the scenarios, with a probability-weighted outcome of 1.5x and 40% of the weight sitting in cases that return less than the money put in [C11].
What we watch

Any confidential S-1 filing signal or a quoted secondary bid on Forge, and any strategic investment or commercial agreement from Ericsson, Nokia, Cisco, HPE or Zebra that would mark a buyer rather than a builder [S4, S5].
Mitigation
No structural mitigation exists. With no vehicle or terms on file there is no redemption right, no transfer provision and no liquidity mechanism of any kind.
Likelihood
Medium: the illiquidity is certain today; whether it persists past 2030 depends on commercial traction that cannot yet be observed.
Risk Rating
6/10: it does not change the business outcome, but it removes every chance to act on one.

text.en: Risk 7: Financial and legal control of a $1B+ company cannot be located: no CFO and no general counsel is named anywhere.
text.zh: 风险 7：一家估值 10 亿美元以上的公司，其财务与法务把关人无处可寻——任何来源都未指名首席财务官或总法律顾问。

rows.en: Risk Type
Team, governance & regulation
Verdict
Financial and legal control of a $1B+ company cannot be located: no CFO and no general counsel is named anywhere.
Impact
One named director oversees a company with no audit trail and no filings on record, so nothing a data room shows could be checked against an external statement [S6].
Why it matters

A chief financial officer owns the revenue recognition policy; a general counsel owns whether a document is a contract or a letter of intent. Those are precisely the two judgments the $450M+ aggregate turns on, and neither role is named in the launch release, the vendor research, the aggregator profiles or the crowdsourced org chart [S1, S4, S6, S15]. Steve Jurvetson of Future Ventures is the only named director [S1]. Tracxn's filings tab for the company returns no records [S6], so there is no external statement against which any internal figure could be checked. The roster itself is unsettled: Forge and The Org list three further co-founders — Alexander Hooshmand, Jake Levy and Eric Roselli — whom company communications never mention [S5, S15]. For a company that has raised roughly $117M across four rounds [C4] and carries a $1B+ mark, a named finance officer, an audit and a board of three or more is the ordinary standard, and institutional investors normally require it as a condition of the round. The consequence is not that misstatement is likely. It is that the commercial figure deciding the return between 0.28x and 1.26x [C7, C8] rests on a classification nobody outside the company is accountable for, with no route to verify it. That is why this sits beside the disclosure problem rather than inside it: the cure is a governance hire and an audited statement, not a customer announcement.
What we watch
A named CFO or general counsel appointment, an audited financial statement, and board additions beyond the single disclosed director. None had appeared as of September 2026 [S1, S4, S6, S15].
Mitigation
No structural mitigation exists. Without a vehicle or terms there is no board seat, no observer right and no reporting covenant, so disclosure depends entirely on what the company chooses to publish.
Likelihood
Medium: the absence is documented today, and a late-stage company can close it with two hires.
Risk Rating
6/10: it does not break the business, but it removes the means of checking the numbers the case turns on.

text.en: Risk 8: The economics of the business are invisible: pricing, gross margin and burn have never been published.
text.zh: 风险 8：这门生意的经济性完全不可见——定价、毛利率和现金消耗从未公布。

rows.en: Risk Type
Commercialization
Verdict
The economics of the business are invisible: pricing, gross margin and burn have never been published.
Impact
An integration-heavy telecom sale can leave gross margin far below the 75% a software-track infrastructure company needs, which would break the 9x exit multiple the base case uses [C8].
Why it matters

Gross margin is revenue minus the direct cost of delivering it, expressed as a percentage. It decides whether a business is valued as software or as services. ZaiNar charges through network software licences, platform subscriptions, deployment and integration services and usage fees [S4]. The first two are software; the third is labour. If deployment and integration hold a large share of contract value — common when a product must be qualified against each customer's radio network before it works — gross margin lands in the 40-60% band of a systems-integration business rather than above 75%. No gross margin, EBITDA or burn figure exists in any source [S4, S9], so where it actually sits is unknown. The consequence runs straight into the valuation. The base case applies a 9x revenue multiple to $200M of 2030 revenue for an exit value of $1.8B, which after 30% dilution returns 1.26x on the $1B entry [C8]. A 9x multiple is a software-infrastructure multiple; a services-weighted business at 45% gross margin would not receive it. At 4x, the same $200M of revenue produces an $800M exit, and after dilution the investor gets back roughly half the money. The unpublished margin is therefore not a detail of quality — it is the input that decides whether the base case is a modest gain or a loss.
What we watch
A published gross margin figure, or pricing disclosed per site or per square metre with the deployment cost stated separately. Neither has been published since the February 2026 launch [S4].
Mitigation

The no-new-hardware architecture is the genuine mechanism: with no tags or anchors to manufacture and ship, the cost of goods is software and services rather than hardware [S1, S4]. That removes one cost layer; it does not show where the remaining integration cost sits.
Likelihood
Medium: telecom-adjacent enterprise deployments typically carry heavy integration, though a licence-led model can still reach software margins.
Risk Rating
5/10: meaningful and directly tied to the exit multiple, but it moves the base case rather than determining survival.

text.en: Risk 9: No one sizes the market ZaiNar actually sells into, because every published total bundles the hardware this model avoids.
text.zh: 风险 9：没有人测算过 ZaiNar 真正销售的那块市场，因为所有已发布的总量都包含了该模式刻意规避的硬件。

rows.en: Risk Type
Market
Verdict
No one sizes the market ZaiNar actually sells into, because every published total bundles the hardware this model avoids.
Impact
The software-only slice of the $18.35B 2026 pool is an assumption, not a figure, so any share-based revenue path is built on sand [C6].
Why it matters

The indoor location market — hardware, software and services for tracking people and assets inside buildings — is put at $18.35B in 2026 and $50.10B by 2031, a 22.3% compound annual growth rate, by MarketsandMarkets [S10]. Checking the arithmetic, $18.35B compounded at 22.3% for five years gives $50.2B, which matches the published 2031 figure [C6]. The growth is real and the demand behind it is documented: an ABI Research survey found 87% of enterprises had not deployed a real-time location system, citing cost, complexity and reliability, with 56% preferring 5G positioning [S17]. The problem is composition. Those totals include tags, anchors, installation and maintenance — the hardware and services a software-only layer does not sell — and no published report isolates the software slice. That matters because the usual way to build a revenue path is to take a market total and apply a share. Here the total is the wrong base, so any share applied to it produces a number with no meaning. The honest response is the one the scenarios take: the 2030 revenue lines of $200M and $500M are stated as assumptions about what a site-by-site sales motion can deliver [C8, C9], not derived from a share of category. A reader should treat the $50.10B ceiling as evidence that the category is worth attacking and as nothing more.
What we watch

A syndicated report that separates software and platform revenue from hardware within indoor location, and disclosed average contract value per site from any vendor in the category. Neither exists in the sources reviewed as of September 2026 [S10, S11].
Mitigation

Treating the published totals as a ceiling rather than a target is the real control: the revenue paths in the scenarios are built bottom-up from the sales motion instead of from a share of category [C6, C8].
Likelihood
Medium: the sizing gap is a present fact, though it constrains what we can measure more than what the company can sell.
Risk Rating
5/10: it removes a valuation anchor rather than creating a loss, and the scenarios already avoid relying on it.

text.en: Risk 10: The performance claims that justify the premium have never been tested by anyone outside the company.
text.zh: 风险 10：支撑溢价的性能宣称从未经过公司之外任何一方的检验。

rows.en: Risk Type
Technology
Verdict
The performance claims that justify the premium have never been tested by anyone outside the company.
Impact

Sub-meter and sub-10cm accuracy are company-reported with no independent field benchmark as of August 2026 [S4]; if real-world accuracy matches standardized RAN positioning, the differentiator disappears.
Why it matters

Positioning accuracy is the error between computed and true location, and it degrades in exactly the conditions that matter: metal-dense factory floors, moving people, congested radio spectrum. A laboratory figure and a hospital-corridor figure are different numbers. ZaiNar reports sub-meter and, in some conditions, sub-10cm accuracy, and Sacra records that as of August 2026 no independent field benchmark had been published [S4]. The company-type test here is to reject any performance claim untethered from the cost advantage it produces: accuracy only pays if it lets a customer retire hardware or automate a workflow, and that link is untested without a measured deployment. What is checkable is that the underlying technique exists — US10455350B2, a granted radiolocation asset-tracking method over a mesh network, names co-founder and CTO Philip Kratz's approach in the public patent record [S5, S14]. A granted patent proves the method was novel to the patent office. It does not prove field accuracy. The consequence connects to Risk 3: if measured real-world performance sits at the decimeter level Ericsson and MediaTek demonstrated over a commercial network in August 2026 [S4], the premium over standardized positioning is zero and the pricing power the base case assumes is gone. This rates below the standards risk because the estate and the nine-year development history make the capability plausible; it is the margin of advantage, not its existence, that is unverified.
What we watch
A published third-party accuracy benchmark in a live deployment, and any customer-side measurement from the Tokyo Metropolitan Government program selected in April 2026 [S3, S4].
Mitigation

The granted patent record is a partial check: US10455350B2 independently confirms the positioning method exists and is attributable to the named inventor, even though it says nothing about field accuracy [S14].
Likelihood
Medium: nine years of development and a granted estate make the capability plausible, while the size of the advantage remains unmeasured.
Risk Rating
5/10: it erodes pricing power if the advantage proves small, but it is bounded by evidence that the underlying method works.

text.en: 3. Disconfirming evidence

The strongest facts run against the pass, and they all attack the same point: that the missing disclosure means the business is not there. Each is weighed below, and each is weighed against Risk 1 — the commercial figure that cannot be read as revenue — because that is the risk they would have to defeat.

items.en: The patent estate is real, checkable in part, and puts a floor under the downside. ZaiNar reports 100+ filings and 90+ issued patents with zero rejections in phase-based time synchronization and network-computed positioning as of February 2026, and US10455350B2 is a granted, publicly viewable record naming the underlying method with CTO Philip Kratz as inventor [S1, S5, S14]. That cuts against a pass because it means nine years of stealth produced a transferable asset rather than a prototype, and a buyer would pay for it even if the product never scales. It is also why the bear case is a $400M trade sale returning 0.28x rather than a write-off [C7] — the estate moves the floor, and it is the main reason the risk-reward dimension scores above the minimum. It does not move the entry price, which is what the pass is about.

The demand gap is documented by someone other than the company, and the category is compounding fast. An ABI Research survey found 87% of enterprises had not deployed a real-time location system, citing cost, complexity and reliability, with 56% preferring 5G positioning [S17] — that is exactly the objection a no-new-hardware software layer answers. The indoor location category runs from $18.35B in 2026 to $50.10B by 2031, a 22.3% annual rate [S10, C6]. Against the pass, this says the problem is real and the buyer intent is independent of ZaiNar's own marketing. The survey is dated June 2021, and a large market with documented demand is a reason a company could succeed, not evidence that this one is selling.

The capital and ecosystem behind the company are the kind that open the exact door the model needs. SoftBank, Samsung, AME Cloud Ventures, Evolution VC Partners and Alchemist Accelerator appear on the round-by-round register, alongside Future Ventures with Steve Jurvetson on the board, and the company holds a seat in the Arm Total Design ecosystem for location awareness in physical AI [S1, S8, S16]. That is carrier- and silicon-adjacent capital rather than only generalist money, and it is the credible route to the distribution Risk 5 says is missing. The counterweight is that seven months after the launch promised carrier partnerships within weeks, none has been announced [S1, S4].

A government selected the company on competitive review, which is the one third-party judgment on file. The Tokyo Metropolitan Government chose ZaiNar as one of seven companies from applicants across 22 countries for its GX market-entry support program in April 2026 [S3]. A competitive selection by a public body is harder to manufacture than a press release, and it cuts against the claim that no outside party has tested the company. It is a market-entry support program with no disclosed contract value, so it evidences access to Tokyo rather than a production deployment or revenue.

Seven months out of a nine-year stealth is early, and the absence of financial disclosure may say little about the finances. A company that spent nine years building before announcing anything has no habit of quarterly disclosure, and private companies at this stage routinely withhold revenue and margin from the public record. Read that way, the gaps are a communications posture rather than a signal about performance. The reason this does not change the call: the price is already set at $1B+, the commercial figure the company chose to publish is the one it blended, and the return at that price is 1.26x over four years even in the case where everything works [C8]. A pass on the mark as disclosed can be reversed the moment the split is published — it costs nothing to wait, and paying now costs the difference between 1.26x and 0.28x [C7, C8].

text.en: The downside is bounded but expensive. If standards absorb the capability and most of the aggregate lapses as memoranda that never convert, a trade sale to a network incumbent at $400M returns 0.28x after 30% dilution, a 27% annual loss across four illiquid years [C7]. That branch carries 40% of the probability weight, the same weight as the base case, and the probability-weighted outcome of 1.5x leans on the 20% bull branch for more than half its value [C11]. This dimension scores 2 of 3.
1. Scorecard

ZaiNar scores 52 of 100, and the shortfall is concentrated in the two dimensions that decide whether money is made: what the company earns, and what it costs to buy. The scorecard weights nine dimensions to a hundred points; each score below is the one argued in the section that owns it, and the one-line reason is that section's conclusion.

text.en: The pattern matters more than the total. ZaiNar scores adequately wherever the question is about technology and people — 12 of 18 on moat, 6 of 10 on team and governance — and poorly wherever the question is about money. Revenue growth and quality takes 4 of 15 and business model and unit economics 6 of 15, together 10 of the 30 points that measure whether the company earns anything; valuation takes 3 of 8. Those three dimensions carry 38 of the 100 available points and return 13. A company can be genuinely good and still be a poor investment at a given price, and that is what this distribution describes.

None of the weak scores reflects a judgment that the company has failed. They reflect an absence: no revenue, ARR or bookings figure appears in any source reviewed [S4, S9], and the $1B+ post-money announced on 19 February 2026 therefore has nothing underneath it to divide by [S1, C3]. Absence of disclosure nine years after founding and seven months after a public launch is itself evidence, and it is the evidence the score is built on.
2. What decides it
Six questions settle this one. Two get a clean yes, and neither of them is about the business earning money.

items.en: Is the technology real and owned? Yes — 90+ issued patents with zero rejections in phase-based time synchronization and network-computed positioning, company-reported at the 19 February 2026 launch, with US10455350B2 publicly viewable at the patent office and CTO Philip Kratz named on it [S1, S14].

Is the market big enough to matter? Yes — indoor location runs $18.35B in 2026 to $50.10B by 2031, 22.3% a year, and healthcare compounds at 27.8% [S10, S11]. The qualification is that both totals include the tags and anchors this software model does not sell, so the serviceable slice is an assumption rather than a published number [C6].

Do customers buy it? No — no named commercial customer appears anywhere nine years after founding, and Sacra states plainly that as of August 2026 there were no named customers and no independent field benchmarks [S4]. One named production reference with a contract value and a live deployment would flip this.

Is the $450M+ commercial figure revenue? No — it blends signed contracts with non-binding memoranda of understanding, and no source splits the two [S1, S4]. A stated binding-backlog figure, separated from memoranda and dated, would flip it.

Does the price leave room to make money? No — the base case returns 1.26x over four years, about 6% a year, because the exit is being bought at a mark with no revenue denominator [C8, C3]. An entry at or below the $0.6B to $1.3B band's midpoint, or a disclosed revenue line that makes the mark testable, would flip it.

Is there a credible route out? Qualified — the patent estate makes a trade sale to Ericsson, Nokia, Cisco, HPE Aruba or Zebra plausible, but those are the same incumbents that can bundle positioning into contracts customers already hold [S4]. Forge shows no IPO filing signal and no quoted secondary price as of 20 August 2026 [S5]. A confidential filing, or an acquisition of a comparable positioning asset at a revenue multiple, would firm this up.

text.en: The two questions answered yes are the ones a buyer of intellectual property asks. The three answered no are the ones a buyer of a business asks. At a $1B+ mark the price is a price for the business, and the business is the part that has not been shown.
3. Recommendation

body.en: Recommendation: pass on ZaiNar — a $1B+ mark carries no disclosed revenue, no named commercial customer nine years after founding, and a $450M+ headline that blends signed contracts with non-binding memoranda of understanding.

items.en: Entry mark: $1.0B+ post-money, announced 19 February 2026 on a $100M+ raise [S1]. No exact raise amount, share price or post-money is published, so ownership and dilution cannot be derived from public sources. No BSH vehicle or terms are on file (pipeline stage: sourcing).

Base case: $200M of 2030 revenue at a 9x software-infrastructure multiple gives a $1.8B exit; after 30% dilution that is 1.26x on the entry mark, about 6% a year [C8]. Weighting the three cases returns 1.5x, and the cases below 1x carry 40% of the weight [C11].
Holding period: 4 years, entry 2026 to a 2030 exit.

Exit route: trade sale to a network or enterprise-infrastructure incumbent — Ericsson, Nokia, Cisco, HPE Aruba, Zebra — with no IPO filing signal and no quoted secondary price as of 20 August 2026 [S4, S5].

Fair value range: $0.6B to $1.3B on priced-round precedent alone — the corroborated August 2021 Series A post-money of $579.37M at the low end, and 30% added to the February 2026 mark for the new cash and the issued patents at the high end [C2].

text.en: The pass is a judgment about price and proof, not about the technology. Nine years of stealth produced a granted patent estate rather than a prototype, and that estate is what an acquirer would actually be buying [S1, S14]. Enterprises want indoor location and mostly still do not have it, and the category is compounding above 20% a year [S10, S17]. The backers and the ecosystem seat are the kind that open carrier and silicon doors, which is the distribution this model needs [S8, S16]. All three are real, and none of them is a reason to pay $1B+ for an unmeasurable revenue line.

Four risks carry the decision, each argued in full above. The headline commercial figure cannot be read as revenue, because it blends signed contracts with non-binding memoranda and names no customer; if the binding share is small, the bear case becomes the base case and the position returns 0.28x — a loss of roughly three quarters of the money even though the technology works [C7]. The entry price has no denominator: a $1B+ mark sits on revenue that has never been disclosed, and the base case returns 1.26x over four years, about 6% a year [C8] — thin for an illiquid private position, and every point of multiple compression comes out of principal first. Standardization can absorb the product, because RAN-native positioning is already shipping and already accurate; if 3GPP Release 18/19 positioning becomes good enough, the patent estate is worth what an acquirer pays for defensive IP, which is the $400M bear exit rather than a revenue multiple [C7]. And incumbents give away positioning inside licences customers already pay for, so the addressable pool narrows to precision-sensitive workflows and the $50.10B 2031 category ceiling overstates what a standalone vendor can win [C6].

Three disclosures would move the number, and all three are things the company could publish without a data room. A binding-versus-memorandum split of the $450M+ aggregate would turn the strongest commercial claim into a testable one. A named production customer, with a deployment and a contract value, would show that buyers choose this over what their network vendor already bundles. A signed carrier agreement would replace a one-enterprise-at-a-time sales motion with distribution, which is the difference between the $200M base-case revenue line and the $500M bull line [C8, C9]. Absent those, the price asks for conviction that the disclosure does not support.

4. Monitoring & triggers

A pass here is a pass on the mark as disclosed, not a view that the company cannot become investable. Four indicators would change the verdict, and each has a threshold that can be observed from outside the company.

title.en: What changes the verdict

rows.en: Binding backlog, split from memoranda
$450M+ at launch, restated $500M+ in April 2026, with no split disclosed [S1, S3, S4]
A disclosed binding figure above roughly a third of the aggregate, dated and attributable
Re-open at the prevailing mark; a testable backlog is what makes the 9x base-case multiple defensible [C8]
Named production customer
None; the only named counterparty is the Tokyo Metropolitan Government market-entry selection of April 2026 [S3, S4]
One named enterprise deployment live in healthcare or industrial, with a contract value
Raise industry position from 8 of 15 and revisit at a mark inside the $0.6B to $1.3B band [C2]
Carrier distribution agreement
Not signed — promised within weeks in February 2026 and unannounced since [S1, S4]
A signed, named tier-1 carrier or major enterprise-network vendor agreement
Re-underwrite toward the $500M 2030 revenue path, which is where the 4.20x bull case lives [C9]
Standards absorption of RAN-native positioning
Ericsson launched integrated 5G Advanced location services in January 2026 and showed decimeter accuracy with MediaTek in August 2026 [S4]
A commercial 3GPP Release 18/19 deployment matching ZaiNar's accuracy without proprietary middleware
Close the file — the moat becomes defensive IP and the $400M bear exit becomes the reference case [C7]
Financial and legal officers on record
One named director; no CFO, controller or general counsel named anywhere [S1, S15]
A named CFO and general counsel, and an audited statement
Treat any later data room as checkable; without them nothing shown could be tested externally [S6]

text.en: The first three triggers all work in the same direction and none requires a new financing to observe. A binding split, a named deployment and a carrier signature together would move revenue growth and quality off 4 of 15, lift industry position, and give the valuation a denominator — which is three of the four weak dimensions at once. The fourth trigger runs the other way and is the one to watch hardest, because it is already in motion: every quarter that standardized positioning closes the accuracy gap makes the patent estate worth less as a product and more as defensive inventory.

Two of those disclosures could arrive within a quarter of a company that wanted to make them. Until they do, the position asks for four years of illiquidity, a 1.26x base case [C8], and a 40% weight on cases that lose money [C11]. That is the trade, and it is not one to take at this mark.
